Keywords: The

outputs.L1: A method for content distribution within an indoor space and its surrounding area covered by beacon signals. The method includes: setting general data for the content; setting at least one location within the indoor space, including one or a combination of active and inactive locations and other relevant information available in a system; assigning beacons that trigger the content within the indoor space; receiving, by the system from a portable device via a first communication channel, beacon information received by the portable device from a beacon via a second communication channel, wherein the first communication channel is different from the second communication channel; setting one or more events that initiate the content within the indoor space; setting a condition formula for the content that must be fulfilled to qualify for the content; and setting one or more results of the content that are provided when the condition formula is fulfilled.
outputs.L2: A content delivery process is provided for an indoor environment and its nearby area where beacon signals are available. The process involves defining the content’s general information; specifying one or more locations within the indoor space, which may include active locations, inactive locations, or a combination of both, along with other related information accessible in the system; linking beacons that cause the content to be activated in the indoor space; and having the system receive, through a first communication channel from a portable device, beacon data that the portable device obtained from a beacon through a second communication channel, where the first and second communication channels are not the same. The process also includes defining one or more events that start the content within the indoor space, establishing a condition expression that must be satisfied in order for the content to be eligible, and specifying one or more content outcomes to be delivered when the condition expression is met.
outputs.L3:
The method is designed to distribute content within an indoor space and, where applicable, in a surrounding area that is covered by beacon signals. By using beacon-based location awareness, the system can determine when a portable device is near specific areas or points of interest and can provide content that is relevant to that location.

The system first establishes general content data to be delivered to users. This content may include information, notifications, advertisements, instructions, media, or other digital materials. In addition, the system defines at least one relevant indoor location associated with the content. These locations may be designated as active or inactive, depending on whether they are currently intended to trigger content delivery. An active location may be used to initiate content distribution, while an inactive location may be stored in the system but temporarily excluded from triggering any output.

Beacons are then assigned to the relevant indoor locations. Each beacon transmits a signal that can be detected by a portable device, such as a smartphone, tablet, or wearable device. When the portable device detects a beacon signal, the beacon may serve as a trigger for delivering content associated with the corresponding indoor location. In this way, the system links physical locations within the indoor environment to digital content outputs.

The system receives beacon information from the portable device through a communication channel that is different from the channel used for communication between the beacon and the portable device. For example, while the beacon may communicate with the portable device using a short-range wireless signal, the portable device may transmit the detected beacon information to the system through a separate network connection, such as a cellular network, Wi-Fi, or another data communication channel. This allows the system to process beacon detections remotely and determine the appropriate response.

The method also defines events, condition formulas, and resulting content outputs. An event may occur when a portable device detects a specific beacon, enters or exits a defined indoor location, remains within a beacon-covered area for a certain period, or satisfies another predefined trigger. Condition formulas are used to evaluate whether the requirements for delivering content have been met. These conditions may depend on factors such as beacon identity, location status, user profile, time, frequency of visits, prior interactions, or combinations of such criteria.

When the defined conditions are fulfilled, the system provides the corresponding content output to the portable device or otherwise makes it available to the user. The resulting content may be displayed, played, downloaded, or activated according to the rules associated with the event. Through this process, the method enables targeted and context-aware content distribution based on beacon detection and predefined logical conditions within an indoor environment.
outputs.L4:
A content distribution method is provided for delivering information, promotions, notifications, media, instructions, or other content to users within indoor spaces and in surrounding areas covered by beacon signals. The method involves configuring content data to be distributed, defining one or more physical or logical locations associated with that content, and associating the content with beacon-based triggers that can be detected by portable user devices. The portable devices may include smartphones, tablets, wearable devices, or other mobile computing devices capable of detecting beacon signals and communicating with a content distribution system.

In operation, a plurality of beacons may be installed or otherwise positioned throughout an indoor environment, such as a retail store, shopping mall, airport, museum, office building, hospital, stadium, hotel, university campus, or transportation facility. Additional beacons may also be placed in nearby or surrounding areas, such as entrances, parking areas, corridors, sidewalks, transit stops, or other approach zones. Each beacon may transmit beacon information, such as a beacon identifier, location-related data, signal strength data, proximity information, or other trigger information. When a portable device detects beacon information, the device may transmit the detected information to a server, platform, or content management system through one or more communication channels that are distinct from the beacon transmission channel. For example, the beacon may transmit using Bluetooth Low Energy or another short-range wireless protocol, while the portable device may communicate with the content distribution system using Wi-Fi, cellular data, near-field communication, or another network connection.

The method includes configuring event initiators that determine when content distribution should be considered or activated. Event initiators may include detecting a particular beacon, entering or leaving a defined beacon zone, remaining in a location for a specified period of time, approaching a specific area, passing through a sequence of locations, interacting with a user interface, scanning a code, making a purchase, joining a queue, or satisfying another predefined event. The system may evaluate the beacon information received from the portable device together with the configured event initiators to determine whether content should be delivered.

The method may also include applying eligibility conditions before content is distributed. Eligibility conditions may be based on location, proximity, time, date, user profile, user preferences, language, device type, prior user behavior, purchase history, membership status, access rights, campaign limits, inventory status, environmental conditions, or combinations of such factors. For example, a user standing near a particular exhibit in a museum may receive related multimedia content, while a shopper entering a specific department of a store may receive a targeted offer only if the user is eligible for the offer and has not previously received it. Similarly, a traveler approaching a gate at an airport may receive boarding information or directions based on the traveler’s current location and itinerary.

After determining that the appropriate beacon trigger, event initiator, and eligibility conditions have been satisfied, the system generates one or more result outputs. The result outputs may include sending content to the portable device, displaying a notification, opening an application page, presenting a coupon, playing audio or video, providing navigation instructions, updating a user record, triggering an external system, recording an analytics event, or modifying future content delivery rules. The output may be delivered immediately, delayed until a later time, or scheduled according to a campaign or workflow configuration.

By using beacon information received from portable devices through separate communication channels, the method allows an indoor content distribution system to identify user proximity and movement within areas where satellite-based positioning may be inaccurate or unavailable. The method supports highly targeted, contextual, and automated content delivery based on where a user is located, what event has occurred, and whether the user satisfies predetermined conditions. As a result, content can be distributed more efficiently and with greater relevance to the user’s immediate environment and circumstances.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest words in the English language, but it plays an important role in communication. It is called the definite article, and it is used to refer to something specific or already known. For example, when we say “the book,” we are talking about a particular book, not just any book.

This simple word helps make sentences clearer. It points the listener or reader toward a certain person, place, object, or idea. In phrases like “the sun,” “the world,” or “the truth,” the word “the” gives importance and focus to what follows.

Although it may seem ordinary, “the” is one of the most common and useful words in English. Without it, many sentences would sound incomplete or unclear. It shows that even the smallest words can have great meaning.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for a method of distributing content in an indoor location using beacon signals and portable devices.
counterfactuals.output: A method for distributing content within an indoor location includes transmitting, by one or more beacon devices positioned in the indoor location, beacon signals comprising beacon identification information. A portable electronic device detects at least one beacon signal and determines proximity information associated with the corresponding beacon device. The portable electronic device transmits the beacon identification information, proximity information, and optionally user or device context information to a content distribution server. The content distribution server selects content associated with a location or zone of the indoor location based at least in part on the received information and transmits the selected content to the portable electronic device. The portable electronic device presents the content to a user while the user is located within or near the associated location or zone. The method enables location-specific delivery of information, offers, media, instructions, or interactive content without requiring satellite-based positioning.

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize an invention for indoor beacon-based content delivery, including setup of content data, locations, assigned beacons, trigger events, condition formulas, and resulting content actions.
counterfactuals.output:
The invention describes a system for delivering digital content indoors based on proximity to beacons and satisfaction of configurable trigger conditions.

A content provider first sets up content data, such as advertisements, coupons, messages, media, instructions, or application content. The provider also defines one or more indoor locations, such as stores, rooms, departments, exhibits, aisles, or zones within a building. Each location is associated with one or more beacon devices, for example Bluetooth Low Energy beacons, Wi-Fi beacons, RFID/NFC devices, or similar short-range transmitters.

For each item of content, the system stores assignment information that links the content to specific locations and/or specific beacons. The provider may also define trigger events, such as a user device detecting a beacon, entering a beacon range, leaving a beacon range, remaining within range for a threshold time, moving between beacon zones, or detecting multiple beacons in a particular pattern.

The system further allows condition formulas to be configured. These formulas determine whether a detected trigger event should actually cause content to be delivered. Conditions may include beacon identity, signal strength, distance estimate, dwell time, time of day, date, user profile, prior user behavior, purchase history, device state, location sequence, campaign rules, or combinations of such factors using logical operators such as AND, OR, and NOT.

When a user device detects an assigned beacon, the device or a server evaluates the corresponding trigger event and condition formula. If the formula is satisfied, the system performs a resulting content action. The action may include displaying content on the user device, sending a push notification, opening an app screen, playing audio or video, presenting a coupon, logging an impression, updating a user profile, initiating a workflow, or transmitting instructions to another system.

In summary, the invention provides a configurable indoor content-delivery platform in which content, indoor locations, beacon assignments, trigger events, and conditional rules are defined in advance, and user-specific content actions are automatically executed when beacon-based proximity conditions are met.

counterfactuals.output:
A system and method are provided for delivering context-specific content to mobile devices using indoor proximity beacons. In one embodiment, a plurality of beacon devices are associated with respective physical locations within an indoor environment. A server system stores configuration data defining one or more locations, beacon identifiers associated with such locations, activation states for the beacon devices or locations, triggering events, eligibility conditions, and content or other results to be delivered upon satisfaction of the configured conditions.

A mobile device executing a client application detects a wireless signal transmitted by one or more of the beacon devices and transmits detection information to the server system, the detection information including at least one beacon identifier and information associated with the mobile device or a user of the mobile device. The server system determines, based at least in part on the stored configuration data, whether the detected beacon corresponds to an active location or active event, whether one or more predefined eligibility conditions are satisfied, and whether a configured result is associated with the detected beacon, location, or event.

In response to determining that the applicable activation state, event criteria, and eligibility conditions are satisfied, the server system causes delivery of a result to the mobile device. The result may include digital content, a notification, an offer, instructions, media, a message, an application action, a transaction-related prompt, or another electronically deliverable response. If the applicable conditions are not satisfied, delivery of the result may be withheld, delayed, modified, or replaced with an alternative result.

In certain embodiments, an administrative interface enables configuration of beacon-to-location associations, active and inactive states, event schedules, user or device eligibility rules, result definitions, priority rules, and delivery constraints. The eligibility conditions may include one or more of user profile attributes, device attributes, proximity information, time of day, date, event status, prior interactions, authentication status, purchase history, location history, campaign membership, or consent status.

Accordingly, the disclosed system enables indoor beacon-triggered delivery of mobile content in which configurable locations, activation states, events, eligibility conditions, and results are evaluated before content or other actions are provided to a mobile device.
